problem: Existing VLM-for-social-navigation work (e.g. VLM-Social-Nav, Social-LLaVA) is evaluated in a few controlled scenarios, on single images or qualitatively. No one has systematically tested whether VLMs understand real, crowded social navigation scenes: spatial relations, motion over time, and human intentions.
motivation: Socially compliant navigation needs accurate scene understanding, yet VLMs are known to be weak at spatial reasoning. The paper builds a human-grounded VQA benchmark on real SCAND crowd scenes, with object-centric annotations and multiple human answers per question. This lets it quantify how far VLMs are from humans and from simple rules, and locate the failing capability.
key_idea: SocialNav-SUB is a VQA benchmark of 60 real crowded SCAND scenarios with front-view and BEV pedestrian annotations and 5+ human answers per question. It scores VLMs by their probability of agreeing with the human answer distribution, and compares them against human and rule-based baselines.
insight: All tested VLMs fall below the human oracle and a simple geometry-rule baseline, and spatial and spatiotemporal reasoning are the weakest categories. Supplying human-consensus spatial/spatiotemporal answers as CoT context raises Gemini's social-question PA (e.g. Robot Affected by Person 0.64 to 0.78), so perception is the bottleneck for social reasoning. Waypoint selection improves with human-oracle context (o4-mini 36.1% to 46.3%). CoT helps social reasoning (GPT-4o 0.35 to 0.47), while BEV helps only some models (GPT-4o).
method: Scenario mining: 60 challenging 2.5 s (4 Hz) SCAND segments, ranked by crowd size, number of nearby people and robot lateral motion; 1-13 pedestrians, mean 6.65

Object-centric representation: PHALP monocular tracking gives 3D pedestrian poses, transformed to a global frame with odometry, Kalman-smoothed, and projected into the front view and a BEV as numbered colored circles (ADE 0.67±0.14 m on CODa)

Question set: 4968 multiple-choice questions in 3 categories (spatial, spatiotemporal, social) covering positions, goal obstruction, distance change, robot direction, and robot/person actions (avoid, overtake, ignore, follow, yield)
Human study: 153 Prolific participants, at least 5 answers per question, giving the label distribution plus Human Oracle (majority answer) and Average Human baselines
Metrics: Probability of Agreement (PA) and Consensus-Weighted PA (CWPA), which scales agreement by 1/HA_q so high-consensus questions are penalized more for errors
Rule-based baseline: hand-crafted geometric rules on tracked positions (horizontal-deviation cutoffs, robot-goal line intersection for obstruction, obstruction implies avoid)
VLM protocol: same visual and text format as humans, sequential CoT feeding earlier answers into later questions; ablations on CoT, BEV and GT spatial context; waypoint-selection study

setting.backbone: GPT-4o, Gemini 2.0, Gemini 2.5 (flash), o4-mini, LLaVA-Next-Video (all frozen, zero-shot prompted)
setting.training_data: none (benchmark evaluation of off-the-shelf VLMs, no training)
setting.observation: SCAND front-view RGB image sequences (10 frames at 4 Hz) plus BEV with pedestrian tracks
setting.action_space: multiple-choice VQA answers; waypoint selection among candidate waypoints in the auxiliary study
setting.privileged: none for the VLMs beyond PHALP-estimated pedestrian tracks; the rule-based baseline uses those tracks, and the ablations use human-consensus answers as context

numbers.extra: CoT+BEV prompting; PA vs human answers; not a navigation benchmark
numbers.evidence: Table 1 Average Performance Across Question Categories: o4-mini 0.62 ± 0.01 / 0.82 ± 0.01

numbers_note: Not a standard navigation benchmark. Numbers are the paper's VLM rows on its own benchmark; the human and rule-based baselines are not listed here (Human Oracle PA 0.74, Average Human 0.60, Rule-Based 0.64).
results: The best VLM, o4-mini, reaches PA 0.62 / CWPA 0.82. It trails the Human Oracle (0.74 / 1.0) and the rule-based baseline (0.64 / 0.84), and roughly matches the Average Human (0.60). Models are closest to humans on social reasoning (o4-mini 0.66 vs oracle 0.76) and furthest on spatial and spatiotemporal reasoning.
limitations: Only SCAND university-campus scenes (60 scenarios); limited diversity
Only a few VLMs evaluated (Gemini 2.5 flash and o4-mini rather than larger variants), with a single query per question
BEV and tracks depend on noisy PHALP estimates (0.67 m ADE), and the waypoint-selection study is preliminary
